text:
janet_customer: Hey support — long chat responses keep truncating for our web client. We get the first 1-2 tokens then silence, the rest never arrives. Request id: req_01H7A2BC34. Happening from staging behind Fastly. Cc @eli_support

eli_support: sorry you're hitting this, can you paste the exact curl you used? Also is this SSE or websocket?

janet_customer: SSE. Example I used: `curl -v -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-...\" -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream\" -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}] }'`
It works from my laptop but fails from staging behind Fastly.

nora_devx: @janet_customer can you include request headers and the exact x-request-id you see in our logs? Also try `--no-buffer` or `stdbuf -oL` to avoid curl buffering.

janet_customer: server returned header `x-request-id: req_01H7A2BC34`. Nginx access log snippet:
```
10.0.0.5 - - [03/Nov/2025:14:05:21 +0000] \"POST /v1/chat/stream HTTP/1.1\" 200 512 \"-\" \"curl/7.83.1\" rt=0.121 request_id=req_01H7A2BC34 upstream_time=0.11
```

eli_support: thanks. @maria_sre can you check edge/proxy behavior? Might be header flush or chunked transfer buffering. Also can you ask customer for tcpdump or ngrep capture of the stream?

maria_sre: looking at edge logs for req_01H7A2BC34 — connection was long-lived, we saw periodic keepalives but a couple of 0-byte writes reported by Fastly between chunks. Could be proxy buffering/compression. @janet_customer please run:
```
ngrep -d any -W byline port 443 host api.redwood.ai and 'POST'
```
or capture raw bytes via curl:
```
curl -v --no-buffer -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-...\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream test"}]}' \
  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream\" > raw_sse.bin
xxd -g 1 raw_sse.bin | head -n 200
```

ashwin_eng: client-side TCP_NODELAY or proxy Nagle interactions can aggregate small SSE events. For websocket try `websocat -t 'wss://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/ws' -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...'` to see if frames arrive continuously.

janet_customer: ran `curl --no-buffer` from staging behind Fastly, same partial output. raw_sse.bin shows first event with `data: "Hello"` then nothing. Request id still req_01H7A2BC34. Included trimmed tcpdump: 
```
13:05:21.123456 IP staging-proxy > api.redwood.ai: Flags [P.], seq 1:512, ack 1, win 64240
13:05:21.124000 IP api.redwood.ai > staging-proxy: Flags [.], ack 512, win 65535
13:05:21.200000 IP api.redwood.ai > staging-proxy: Flags [P.], seq 512:720, ack 1  # next chunk never seen by client
```

eli_support: interesting. Can you run curl with `--raw --no-buffer` and include `-H 'Accept: text/event-stream'`? Also share model name and prompt length; large KV cache sometimes delays flush.

nora_devx: here's a standard debug cURL we use (please run from staging host and attach outputs):
```
curl -v -N -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-test\" \
  -H \"Accept: text/event-stream\" \
  -H \"x-client-id: staging-42\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream test"}]}' \
  \"https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/stream\" > debug_sse.txt
```
Then run `strace -f -e write curl ...` to see if the client flushes writes.

maria_sre: requested raw TLS logs from Fastly for req_01H7A2BC34 and checked Fastly metrics near 14:05Z — a spike in backpressure and a few reported 0-byte writes. Also checking if gzip compression is enabled for this path; that can block small chunk flushes.

ashwin_eng: if possible, try bypassing Fastly with `--resolve` to hit origin IP directly. If direct works but Fastly fails, that confirms edge buffering.

janet_customer: good call — I ran `curl --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:54.12.34.56 ...` (origin IP) and the stream completed fine. Direct request id was req_01H7A2BC35. So issue only when going through Fastly.

maria_sre: Fastly config has a streaming toggle and chunked encoding behavior. I'll open a ticket with Fastly including request ids (req_01H7A2BC34) and the tcpdump/curl outputs. As a short-term workaround, use websocket or bypass Fastly for staging.

eli_support: next steps: 1) open Fastly ticket with logs and captures; 2) give customer workaround + curl/websocat examples; 3) follow-up when Fastly confirms config change.

janet_customer: switching to websocket for now — thanks :thumbsup: 

deploy-bot: deployment finished: edge-flag/fastly-streaming-toggle rolled out to staging at 2025-11-03T15:10Z

maria_sre: after toggle, we no longer see 0-byte writes for similar requests. Please retest and include new request ids.

janet_customer: retested after rollout — streaming completes. New req id req_01H7A2BC36. All good, closing.
